Ananyiv New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Ananyiv, Ukraine

Not demolished. Founded after WWII, this cemetery received some earlier tombstones relocated from Ananyiv's older cemetery. Jews settled there in the early 19th century, opening a synagogue and cemetery immediately; a Hevra Kadisha operated from 1837. Population reached 532 by 1856 and 3,257 (20%) by 1897, supporting a Jewish government vocational school and a private women's vocational school by century's end; five synagogues and two Jewish cemeteries operated by the early 20th century. A severe April 27, 1881 pogrom damaged 175 Jewish houses, the first of a series repeated in 1905 and 1919 (the latter organized by Ukrainian National Republic Directory forces). Population peaked at 4,817 (22%) by 1910, falling to 3,516 (19%) by 1926 and 1,779 (31%) by WWII's start. An early-1920s Jewish self-defense detachment of 300 members lost 220 in battle against Tyutyunnik's forces; several synagogues operated into the 1930s, though the Jewish school closed in 1934. Nazi occupation saw 300 Jews shot on August 28, 1941, followed by a September 3 ghetto and October deportations to Transnistria; roughly 3,700 Jews were murdered during the 1941-1944 occupation. A 1995 memorial marks the execution site; about 30 Jews remained in Ananyiv by 1998.
